subject.title: fix: preserve embedded prompt caching across room events and native Responses

question: Should ambient room events and unauthorized or unknown senders see the schemas for `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`, relying on the new pre-execution wrapper for denial, while owners and trusted internal cron, heartbeat, and memory turns may execute them?
rationale: The latest head defines coherent trust classes, but schema visibility and owner ambient denial are intentional product and security choices that source inspection and tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the proposed classes
options.body: Keep stable visible schemas, allow owners and trusted internal turns, deny ambient, non-owner, and unknown turns before hooks and implementations, then re-review the resolved head.

options.title: Preserve current disclosure behavior
options.body: Continue filtering denied schemas and revise the cache fix so capability disclosure does not change.

options.title: Split independent fixes
options.body: Separate native continuation and reply-delivery fixes from the protected-tool policy redesign.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed classes
